prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not start a centrally acting anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) for the tremor at 67: high risk of confusion and memory impairment
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with decrement and right-predominant rest tremor with re-emergence and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; the mild postural tremor does not change this; olfactory loss on a validated test (UPSIT 18/40, in the anosmic range, when tested) is a second supportive criterion and makes it clinically established, otherwise the response to levodopa may add one [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]
Measure lying and standing blood pressure during levodopa titration, since amlodipine adds to orthostatic falls
Refer to physiotherapy for gait initiation, turning and the two near-falls, occupational therapy for fine-motor tasks, and speech and language therapy for the hypophonia [NICE_NG71]

interactions: Amlodipine lowers standing blood pressure and adds to the orthostatic fall; levodopa can lower it further. Review the need for each and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each levodopa dose step.
warnings: Metformin, rosuvastatin and pantoprazole: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa.

Dopaminergic drugs can cause somnolence and sudden sleep onset: counsel about driving.
Impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, binge eating) occur mainly with dopamine agonists.

patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. Arjun Mehta is a 67-year-old right-handed retired civil engineer who presents to the outpatient neurology clinic accompanied by his wife for evaluation of a gradually progressive right hand tremor and generalized slowing over the past 18 months. He first became aware of an intermittent tremor in his right hand approximately 18 months ago, initially noticed while sitting quietly at home or during Zoom calls when he was not actively using his hands. The tremor was subtle at first and did not interfere with tasks, but over the subsequent year it became more frequent and prominent. His wife first drew his attention to it approximately 12 months ago when she noticed his right hand shaking on his lap during a family dinner. He reports that the tremor diminishes or temporarily stops when he uses his hand for purposeful tasks but reappears when he brings his arm back to rest.

Over the past year, Mr. Mehta has noticed increasing difficulty with tasks requiring fine motor coordination. Buttoning his dress shirts and formal kurtas has become laborious, particularly the smaller buttons, and he now enlists his wife's help. His handwriting, which he prided himself on for his calligraphy hobby, has become progressively smaller and more cramped; friends have commented that they can barely read his letters. He has abandoned calligraphy entirely in the past three months.

Both the patient and his wife have noticed changes in his walking over the past 12 months. He walks with less swing in his right arm and takes smaller, slower steps than before. He has had two episodes of near-falling when turning quickly, though no actual falls to the ground. He describes a sense of his feet feeling 'heavy' when initiating gait, particularly after sitting for an extended period. His wife notes that his voice has become noticeably softer and that his facial expression seems less animated than it used to be.

Of note, the patient and his wife report that his ability to smell common foods and household odors has been clearly diminished for the past two to three years. He no longer notices the scent of spices cooking or freshly brewed tea, something his wife specifically remarks upon. He initially attributed this to 'getting older.' He denies acting out dreams during sleep, and his wife has not observed any such behavior. He reports some constipation over the past year requiring a fiber supplement. He denies lightheadedness upon standing, hallucinations, cognitive complaints, difficulty swallowing, or urinary urgency beyond mild nocturia. He denies any exposure to antipsychotic medications, antiemetic dopamine blockers, or toxins. There is no history of encephalitis, significant head trauma, or family history of Parkinson's disease.

neurological_exam.additional: Resting tremor observed in the right hand at 4-6 Hz with a pill-rolling quality, present while hands resting in the lap and re-emerging during ambulation. Tremor is suppressed on voluntary movement and re-emerges after a brief latency when the arm is held outstretched (re-emergent tremor). There is also a mild action/postural tremor component of approximately 6-8 Hz noted when arms are extended, most prominent in the right hand. No tremor observed at rest in the left hand. Handwriting sample shows progressive micrographia. Glabellar tap sign positive with failure to habituate after 10 taps (Myerson sign).
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose intact bilaterally without dysmetria. Heel-to-shin testing intact. Rapid alternating movements (finger tapping, hand pronation-supination) show marked decrement in speed and amplitude on the right side with progressive fatiguing over 10 seconds; left side mildly slow but amplitude maintained. No cerebellar features.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, round, and reactive to light bilaterally (3 mm to 2 mm). Extraocular movements full and conjugate without nystagmus. Facial sensation intact bilaterally to light touch and pinprick. Mild hypomimia with reduced spontaneous blink rate (approximately 8 per minute). Hearing grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tongue midline, no fasciculations. Patient reports reduced ability to smell common odors for the past 2-3 years; wife confirms he no longer notices the aroma of freshly brewed tea.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly stooped posture. Reduced right arm swing, left arm swing relatively preserved. Stride length mildly shortened. Initiation slightly hesitant. En bloc turning (requires 4-5 steps). No festination observed. Pull test: one to two steps of retropulsion with self-correction. Tandem gait mildly impaired. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and fully oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Speech is mildly hypophonic with reduced prosody but fluent without paraphasic errors. Comprehension, repetition, and naming intact. Mini-Mental State Examination 29/30 (lost one point on spelling WORLD backwards). Affect mildly flat. No evidence of depression on brief screening. Wife reports no change in cognition or memory.
neurological_exam.motor: Bulk normal throughout. Increased tone in the right upper extremity with cogwheeling at the wrist and elbow, accentuated by contralateral activation maneuver. Mild rigidity at the right ankle. Left upper extremity tone mildly increased at the wrist only. Lower extremity tone slightly increased on the right. Strength 5/5 in all extremities bilaterally. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis, patellar, and Achilles tendons bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Light touch, pinprick, temperature, proprioception, and vibration intact in all extremities. No cortical sensory deficits.
